Pinned upstream API shapes for opendaisugi.model_host.
Fetched 2026-09-08.

ollama_tags.json         https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/api.md
                         Section "List Local Models", GET /api/tags. Verbatim example
                         response.

ollama_show.json         https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/api.md
                         Section "Show Model Information", POST /api/show. Verbatim
                         example response for:
                           curl http://localhost:11434/api/show -d '{"model": "llava"}'
                         CORRECTION: the request body key is "model", not "name". The
                         earlier prose form {"name": m} is stale against the current
                         docs. model_host.py sends {"model": m}.
                         NOTE: num_ctx appears here inside "modelfile", as a
                         "PARAMETER num_ctx 4096" line, and not inside "parameters".
                         The Ollama docs are not consistent about which field carries
                         it. It depends on the model. _ollama_num_ctx() checks both.

openai_models.json       Standard OpenAI /v1/models shape: object, data, id, object,
                         created, owned_by. Partly confirmed for the Ollama OpenAI
                         compatible surface at https://docs.ollama.com/openai, where
                         created is the last modified time and owned_by defaults to
                         "library". That page publishes no full example body. This
                         fixture is the well known OpenAI schema, not a byte for byte
                         copy of a fetched example. Context window extraction from a
                         /v1/models entry is best effort. See model_host._probe_openai.
                         It is not verified against a real llama.cpp or vLLM server.

anthropic_message.json   https://docs.ollama.com/api/anthropic-compatibility
                         Constructed from the page's "Supported response fields" list:
                         id, type, role, model, content, stop_reason, and usage with
                         input_tokens and output_tokens. The page publishes no full
                         example response body. The page confirms: the endpoint is
                         /v1/messages; base_url is documented WITHOUT /v1 because the
                         SDK appends it, for example ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://host:11434;
                         ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama is the documented literal token;
                         the api key is "accepted but not validated"; and
                         /v1/messages/count_tokens is listed as NOT supported. That last
                         fact is the premise of the count-tokens shim in gateway_asgi.py.
